title: Cutting polynomial coordinates on the reduction of a syntomic algebra
statement: Call a map $T\to E$ syntomic if it is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], finitely presented [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and every fibre $E\otimes_T\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a local complete intersection over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]; residue fields are as in [def-weil-residue-field]. Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I\subset R$ any ideal, and $R\to D$ syntomic. Let $A_0$ be a syntomic $R/I$-algebra and fix an $R/I$-algebra isomorphism $\theta:D/ID\xrightarrow{\sim}A_0[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], for $r\ge0$. Choose $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in D$ with $\theta(\bar t_i)=x_i$, and put $A=D/(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$. Then there is $a\in A$ mapping to $1$ under the induced isomorphism $A/IA\cong A_0$ such that $R\to A_a$ is syntomic [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. There are no nilpotence or Noetherian hypotheses; $r=0$ and $A_0=0$ are allowed.

source.place: Tag 07M8 (proposition-lift-smooth), proof of assertion (1), final claim and its proof, starting "Choose f_1,...,f_n in D"; local presentations use algebra.tex Tag 00SY and the appended equations use Tag 00ST.

proof.text: The map $D\to A$ followed by reduction modulo $I$ identifies $A/IA$ with $A_0[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_1,\ldots,x_r)=A_0$: the inverse sends a coefficient to its constant polynomial class. If $D=R[y]/(g)$ is any finite presentation and $t_i$ has polynomial lift $t_i^{\prime}$, then $A=R[y]/(g,t_1^{\prime},\ldots,t_r^{\prime})$. Thus $A$ is finitely presented. These are quotient identities, with no flatness assumption on $R/I$.

source.place: Tag 07M8 (proposition-lift-smooth), proof of (1), paragraph beginning Choose f_1,...,f_n in D

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak q\in V(IA)$ and let $\widetilde{\mathfrak q}$ be its inverse image in $D$, and $\mathfrak p=\widetilde{\mathfrak q}\cap R$. Then $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Flatness of $R\to D$ gives flatness of $R_{\mathfrak p}\to D_{\widetilde{\mathfrak q}}$. The fibre of $D$ is a local complete intersection by hypothesis; its defining principal global-complete-intersection cover contains the fibre prime associated to $\widetilde{\mathfrak q}$. The local syntomic chart theorem therefore supplies $u\notin\widetilde{\mathfrak q}$ and a specified relative global complete intersection presentation $D_u=R[y_1,\ldots,y_N]/(g_1,\ldots,g_c)$. Its quotient by the images of $t_i$ is $A_{\bar u}$.

source.place: Tag 07M8 (proposition-lift-smooth), proof of (1), claim: the question is local on Spec D; use 00SY

proof.text: Put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $B=A_0\otimes_{R/I}k$, a finite type $k$-algebra, since a finite presentation of $A_0$ gives finite generators after scalar extension. Reduction followed by scalar extension identifies $D\otimes_R k$ with $B[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$, sending $t_i$ to $x_i$, and $A\otimes_Rk$ with $B$. Explicitly on tensors the first identification sends $d\otimes\lambda$ to $\theta(\bar d)\otimes\lambda$; it is invertible because $I$ acts by zero on $k$. Let $q_B$ be the fibre prime associated to $\mathfrak q$. The prime associated to $\widetilde{\mathfrak q}$ is $Q=q_BB[x]+(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$. The fibre of $D_u$ is $(B[x])_{u_k}$, with $u_k\notin Q$. Its displayed presentation is a global complete intersection with $N$ variables and $c$ equations, by base change of the relative presentation. Equidimensionality and invariance under an open neighbourhood give $\dim_Q\operatorname{Spec}B[x]=N-c$. The zero-section dimension formula gives $\dim_{q_B}\operatorname{Spec}B=N-c-r$.

source.place: Tag 07M8 (proposition-lift-smooth), proof of (1), claim: compute the fibre dimensions before appending the equations

proof.text: Lift the images of $t_i$ in $D_u$ to polynomials $t_i^{\prime}\in R[y_1,\ldots,y_N]$. Then $A_{\bar u}=R[y]/(g_1,\ldots,g_c,t_1^{\prime},\ldots,t_r^{\prime})$ has $N$ variables and $c+r$ equations. Its fibre dimension at the prime coming from $\mathfrak q$ is $N-(c+r)$: it is the open neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}B_{\bar u_k}$ of $q_B$ in the preceding step. In particular $N\ge c+r$. Apply the pointwise equation-count localization lemma to this specified presentation. It gives $v\notin\mathfrak q A_{\bar u}$ such that $(A_{\bar u})_v$ is a relative global complete intersection. This applies to arbitrary $R$, using the lemma at a point, rather than assuming the entire closed reduction has one constant dimension.

source.place: Tag 07M8 (proposition-lift-smooth), proof of (1), claim: append the lifted equations and apply 00ST(3)

proof.text: Write $v=b/\bar u^e$ in $A_{\bar u}$. Then $(A_{\bar u})_v\cong A_{\bar u b}$: in either ring both $\bar u$ and $b$ are invertible, and their universal localization maps are inverse. Also $\bar u b\notin\mathfrak q$. Consequently, for every $\mathfrak q\in V(IA)$ we have found an element $b_{\mathfrak q}\notin\mathfrak q$ with $A_{b_{\mathfrak q}}$ a relative global complete intersection. This is just fraction arithmetic applied to the charts already obtained, not a further syntomic descent assertion.

source.place: Tag 07M8 (proposition-lift-smooth), proof of (1), claim: express each resulting neighbourhood as a principal neighbourhood in Spec A

proof.text: Let $J\subseteq A$ be the ideal generated by all the $b_{\mathfrak q}$ just obtained. Every prime containing $IA$ misses one of these generators, so $V(J)\cap V(IA)=\varnothing$. The disjoint-zero-loci criterion gives $a\in J$ and $i\in IA$ with $a+i=1$. Thus $a$ maps to $1\in A/IA=A_0$. Choose a finite expression $a=\sum_{j=1}^m h_jb_j$ with each $b_j$ one of the chart elements. In $A_a$, the relation $\sum_j(h_j/a)b_j=1$ gives a finite principal cover. If $V(IA)$ is empty, $J=0$ and the same criterion gives $IA=A$; take $a=0$, giving the zero localization.

source.place: Tag 07M8 (proposition-lift-smooth), proof of (1), after the claim: find a localization equal to 1 on the reduction

proof.text: For each chosen $b_j$, the ring $(A_a)_{b_j}\cong(A_{b_j})_a$ is a relative global complete intersection: the cited principal-localization theorem appends one variable and one equation to a relative global complete intersection presentation, so its dimension difference is unchanged. Apply relative-complete-intersection principal-cover syntomic gluing to $R\to A_a$ and the displayed relation $\sum_j(h_j/a)b_j=1$. It gives flatness, finite presentation and local-complete-intersection fibres of $R\to A_a$, exactly the required syntomicity. The gluing theorem permits the empty cover and the zero algebra. Nothing required $r>0$, $A_0\ne0$, nilpotence of $I$, or Noetherianity of $R$.

source.place: Tag 07M8 (proposition-lift-smooth), proof of (1), after the claim: the localized ring is syntomic
